items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce (BlockStrap RCE)
items.summary: Adobe released a security update addressing multiple vulnerabilities, with the most critical being CVE-2026-103849 (BlockStrap), a template engine injection flaw with a CVSS score of 10.0 that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code. This bulletin also includes fixes for other critical, high, and medium vulnerabilities, such as incorrect authorization and stored cross-site scripting issues.

items.title: SessionReaper: Unauthenticated RCE in Magento & Adobe Commerce
items.summary: Discovered in August 2025, this critical vulnerability (CVSS 9.1) allows customer account takeover and unauthenticated remote code execution under certain conditions. Active mass attacks exploiting SessionReaper were observed starting October 22, 2026, with attackers uploading PHP backdoors as fake sessions.

items.title: StyleSmuggler: Magento and Adobe Commerce 0-day RCE under active attack
items.summary: Sansec discovered StyleSmuggler, a zero-day vulnerability with a CVSS score of 10.0 that enables unauthenticated remote code execution by injecting malicious code into Magento's template system. Attacks began on September 4, 2026, leading Adobe to release an emergency hotfix on September 7, 2026.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce
items.summary: Adobe released a security update resolving critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities that could lead to security feature bypass and privilege escalation. This bulletin also advises applying the hotfix for CVE-2026-75650 in addition to the updates.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce
items.summary: This Adobe security update addresses critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities, including an unauthenticated incorrect authorization flaw (CVE-2026-71362, CVSS 9.1) and two stored cross-site scripting flaws. Successful exploitation could result in security feature bypass, arbitrary code execution, and privilege escalation.

items.title: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type (PolyShell)
items.summary: Adobe fixed this critical vulnerability, named 'PolyShell' by Sansec, which is an unrestricted file upload flaw that could lead to arbitrary code execution. CISA added CVE-2026-48356 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 27, 2026, indicating active exploitation.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization in Adobe Commerce B2B
items.summary: Addressed in APSB26-153, this critical vulnerability affects Adobe Commerce B2B and allows unauthenticated code execution with a CVSS score of 9.8.

items.title: Stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS) with Privilege Escalation
items.summary: This critical vulnerability, part of APSB26-153, is a stored cross-site scripting flaw that can lead to privilege escalation.

items.title: Stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS) with Privilege Escalation
items.summary: Another critical stored cross-site scripting vulnerability addressed in APSB26-153, potentially leading to privilege escalation.

items.title: Stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS)

items.title: Stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS)

items.title: Incorrect Authorization in Adobe Commerce B2B
items.summary: A high-severity incorrect authorization flaw affecting Adobe Commerce B2B, which could result in security feature bypasses, fixed in APSB26-153.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization in Adobe Commerce B2B
items.summary: This high-severity incorrect authorization vulnerability in Adobe Commerce B2B, addressed by APSB26-153, can lead to security feature bypasses.
